study.question: Does averaging neighboring occupied-block preactivations before the inherited tanh improve full-validation click AUC over separated-block averaging and the incumbent, and does that contrast depend on auxiliary adapter-context transfer?
study.hypothesis: Observation: source bests are 0.660646940486458 and 0.660163362657485; the current block nonlinear incumbent reaches 0.6685268680116033, versus aggregate transfer 0.668457307890924. Finer event nonlinear expectation failed to improve it (0.6683746776429751); ordered pair-product summaries (0.668306119347773) also lost to scrambled (0.6685097769484223), and aligned/rotated mass variants did not improve it. These successful executions with weaker predictive results are counterevidence to specific implementations, not failures to execute. The incumbent still applies its nonlinearity separately to each compressed block, so its branch cannot express the nonlinearity of a cross-block average. Proposed explanation, not established: neighboring compressed blocks may share a useful latent interest state; mean-preserving pairing can pool local noise before tanh while retaining long-range variation. Separated pairing has identical pairing multiplicity and capacity but pools distant states. Cross the grouping contrast with the existing auxiliary adapter-context gradient gate to test whether any locality advantage requires auxiliary transfer. The latest event advantage from transfer was only 0.0002531340011854 versus the block transfer difference 0.0006587341379314; these single-seed descriptive interactions are not significance or repeated support. Auxiliary AUCs of the incumbent are below DIN, so this is a click-selected tradeoff, not an established all-task improvement.

study.proposed_difference: For M occupied blocks in chronological supplied-position order let z_j=W_h[M*b_j,r], with unchanged global details r. Pair valid block ranks symmetrically. Adjacent pairs are (0,1),(2,3),...; separated pairs connect rank j to j+E/2 modulo E for the first E=2*floor(M/2) occupied blocks. If M is odd the newest occupied block is a singleton in BOTH pairings. Every paired row replaces z_j by (z_j+z_partner)/2, then the branch averages tanh over the original M occupied rows. Thus paired rows occur twice, both designs retain the same singleton, and the pre-tanh mean equals the original mean; no new length/count weighting is introduced. Packing is based solely on mask validity, supporting noncontiguous inputs. M<=3 gives identical pairings; the distinction first exists at M>=4. Both pairings and the inherited block/aggregate paths execute in every variant, with zero-gradient unused edges. The optional none pairing is only a native host parity diagnostic against the incumbent, not a fifth requested training run. No verified novelty claim is made.
predictions: adjacent_transfer should exceed separated_transfer and the unchanged incumbent on full-population validation click AUC if useful chronological locality survives compression; comparisons to both frozen sources and DIN remain reported.

Define locality effects D_T=AUC(adjacent_transfer)-AUC(separated_transfer) and D_B=AUC(adjacent_blocked)-AUC(separated_blocked). D_T>0 supports the tested locality contrast provisionally; D_T-D_B>0 is the predeclared transfer-dependence contrast, with paired repetition required before a mechanism claim.

At common nonzero weights, both pairings have identical outputs for zero to three occupied blocks and preserve the same pre-tanh mean for all masks; adjacent versus separated can differ for at least four occupied blocks with heterogeneous preactivations. Homogeneous preactivations recover the original block summary. These are mathematical implementation predictions, not learned-outcome claims.

Any direct grouping effect should occur on histories with at least four occupied blocks. Existing history_gt64 and history17_64 slices provide coarse diagnostics; short/empty-history learned metrics may still shift through shared training. Slices are exploratory with counts, not independent samples or alternate selection metrics.

Exactly 32192421 total,31793216 embedding,399205 dense parameters are expected from source inheritance; host must measure. Two pair gather/tanh paths add work versus the incumbent, so no efficiency claim is justified without full measured latency/memory/training cost.
falsifiers: Failure of adjacent_transfer to exceed the incumbent on full-validation click AUC rejects useful improvement for this implementation even if it beats separated_transfer; failure to exceed separated_transfer with paired repeats rejects the tested locality explanation.

Comparable adjacent and separated gains over the incumbent favor generic smoothing/coarsening over chronological locality; an advantage confined to blocked transfer contradicts the proposed positive transfer interaction.

Involution, occupied-support exclusion, newest singleton, same pre-tanh mean, M<=3 equality or homogeneous-limit failure, forbidden auxiliary gradients, parameter/state changes, or nonfinite FP32/BF16 forward/backward invalidate the implementation, not the scientific hypothesis.

A result explained by sparse/dense capacity, native Dice state, masking mistakes, extra passes or unacceptable measured runtime does not establish a quality/cost improvement. One seed cannot resolve small validation gaps after many adaptive trials.
alternative_explanations: Generic variance contraction, reduced tanh saturation or changed gradient magnitude may explain a gain independently of temporal locality.
Recency-sensitive occupancy and the predeclared newest singleton can matter, although singleton policy and multiplicities match between pairing controls.
Existing detail summaries still encode position; comparisons measure local grouping in this branch conditional on those inherited paths, not a global sequence-order ablation.
BF16 summation and shared training change scores/Dice trajectories; numeric common-weight identities do not imply identical learned checkpoints.
Single-seed noise, adaptive validation reuse and stochastic optimization can explain small gaps; repeated validation comparisons and user-cluster uncertainty are necessary before repeated support.
Whole-window filtering/static snapshots and offline historical feedback are inherited benchmark limitations; production causality is unverified.
